title: Drain Slope Myth: Is Steeper Always Better?
description: A common misconception in drainage piping is that increasing the pipe slope will clear waste faster and prevent clogs. In reality, over-sloping horizontal drain lines causes liquids to flow past solid waste too quickly, leaving heavy matter stranded in the pipe. Over time, these stranded solids build up and form severe blockages. Maintaining the code-specified pitch, typically a quarter inch per foot for standard pipe sizes, ensures liquid and solid waste travel together smoothly down the line without separation.
caption:
Drain Slope Myth: Is Steeper Always Better?

A common misconception in drainage piping is that increasing the pipe slope will clear waste faster and prevent clogs. In reality, over-sloping horizontal drain lines causes liquids to flow past solid waste too quickly, leaving heavy matter stranded in the pipe. Over time, these stranded solids build up and form severe blockages. Maintaining the code-specified pitch, typically a quarter inch per foot for standard pipe sizes, ensures liquid and solid waste travel together smoothly down the line without separation.
